sources.publisher: U.S. House of Representatives, History, Art & Archives
sources.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez: biography and congressional service
sources.findings: Read House History concise biography and service table: born 13 October 1989 in the Bronx, BA 2011, service from 3 January 2019, 116th through 119th Congresses. A fourth term in the 119th Congress is not the next term contested in November 2026. Committee institution creation dates are not her personal appointment dates.

sources.title: 2019 Distinguished Alumni Award: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
sources.findings: Read the Boston University Economics 2019 alumni profile under her own heading: BA in International Relations and Economics in 2011, internship in Senator Ted Kennedy’s immigration office, later bartender and waitress work. Gina Ortiz Jones’s adjacent 2003 degrees and military career are not Ocasio-Cortez’s. No postgraduate degree added.

sources.title: About: early life, campaign and first terms
sources.findings: Read the member office’s About biography: community organisation, 2016 Sanders volunteer work, 2018 primary victory and January 2019 entry as the then-youngest woman in Congress. Treat this as an interested office source. Do not turn its advocacy, causal claims or dated programme totals into independent measures of policy effectiveness.

sources.title: Congressional Directory, July 2020: New York, District 14
sources.findings: Read GPO July 2020 Congressional Directory entry: exact birth date, BA year, previous professional roles and general election on 6 November 2018. Historical office staff, addresses, committee assignments and district population are not treated as current. Religion and unnecessary personal data are not copied.

sources.title: 26 June 2018: Joe Crowley defeated in Democratic primary
sources.findings: Read Bridget Bowman’s Roll Call report dated 26 June 2018: AP called the Democratic primary for Ocasio-Cortez over incumbent Joe Crowley, who conceded. The 58–42 figures were at 88 percent reporting, so no final vote share is inferred. Primary nomination, November election and January taking office remain separate.

sources.title: H.Res.109, introduced 7 February 2019: Green New Deal resolution
sources.findings: Read the GPO introduced text of H.Res.109 and its accompanying content-details metadata. Submitted 7 February 2019 and referred to committees. Ten-year mobilisation, emissions, jobs and equity are proposed goals, not achieved outcomes. A House resolution proposal is not an enacted national programme. Congress.gov direct opening failed; the equivalent original GPO text was readable.

sources.publisher: Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives
sources.title: 119th Congress member profile: oath and district
sources.findings: Read the Clerk’s current member profile: New York district 14, Democrat, oath for the 119th Congress on 3 January 2025. Current Energy and Commerce listing agrees with House History, but no unsupported committee leadership title is assigned.

sources.title: 25 July 2025 report: Met Gala gifts, payments and findings
sources.findings: Read July 2025 Ethics Committee report introduction, findings on printed page 25 and conclusion on page 26. Adopted 22 July, released 25 July. It found gift/payment rule violations, no evidence of intentional underpayment, and inadequate staff oversight. No sanction was merited provided she donated $250 for the partner’s meal and paid Brother Vellies an additional $2,733.28. The report says closure follows publication and repayment; no independent receipt or later closure record was verified. Neither the payment nor the report is a criminal fine or conviction. Older allegation-only accounts do not replace the final report.

sources.title: 4 November 2026: reported House reelection, citing AP race calls
sources.findings: Read Anadolu’s 4 November 2026 report citing AP race calls for the previous day’s election, including her retention of New York district 14. This is an attributed media result, not a state-certified return, and the next term had not yet begun. No final vote total or future higher-office candidacy is inferred.

sources.publisher: Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives
sources.title: 12 November 2026, Roll Call 323: Major Richard Star Act
sources.findings: Read the Clerk’s official Roll Call 323 header and individual member row: 12 November 2026, H.R.2102, Major Richard Star Act, Ocasio-Cortez recorded Yea. This supplies recent dated parliamentary activity. A secondary search result associated the same roll number with an Iran war-powers measure; that mismatch is discarded in favour of the primary record. No claim of independently viewing her physical presence or of this House passage alone enacting a law.
